verdict.rationale: ROS 2 provides client-library APIs (C++/Python) with topics/services/actions that let any program—including an AI agent—command a robot end-to-end (ros2-docs-7, ros2-docs-10, ros2-docs-24), and it has a security layer (sros2, DDS-Security, keystores, enclaves) that supports authentication and per-participant policy scoping (ros2-docs-12, ros2-docs-13, ros2-docs-15, ros2-docs-40, ros2-docs-42). However, there is no evidence of an AI-agent-specific credential/token scoping mechanism (e.g., API keys, OAuth-style scopes) or of documented agent-oriented SDK workflows tying authentication directly to command execution. missing for 10: explicit scoped-credential/token issuance for AI agents, agent-specific SDK examples, and independent verification that the security/enclave system is used this way in practice.
